title: No path is made relative across drives, in tests or tools
description: Second instance of the cross-drive relpath class (P132.5 fixed suite_elsewhere_paths; P133.1's gtf-block fixture reintroduced it), so the class is closed by a check, not another instance fix.
desiredOutcome: The release tier is green on Windows, and a relpath between a scratch directory (C:) and the checkout (D:) can no longer be written without a lint naming it.

findings.issue: rel_or_abs(mp10, os.getcwd()) returns the ABSOLUTE path whenever scratch and cwd are on different drives, which is exactly the hosted windows runner (checkout on D:, scratch on C:). i31 then feeds an absolute manifest to a case titled 'an import given a relative manifest ... prints it absolute' and its assertion (isabs(words[2]) and samefile) is trivially true: the case is green on the one machine it was fixed for without exercising the relative-to-absolute conversion. The title now says 'relative here: False', but a title is not an assertion, and nothing makes a green run on that runner read as vacuous. The helper's docstring asks such a caller to check isabs and say so; this one says so only in text.
findings.resolution: fixed in P148.3 (b8c642ec2e6e): Make the case exercise the relative spelling on every drive layout: run the CLI with the working directory moved into os.path.dirname(mp10) (os.chdir in try/finally, M.main runs in-process) and pass os.path.basename(mp10); then no cross-drive question exists. Failing that, assert the 'relative here' leg only when it is relative and record the absolute leg as a separate, honestly-titled case.

findings.issue: os.getcwd() is classified as neither scratch nor checkout, so the exact call the executor wrote to repair i31, relpath(scratch_path, os.getcwd()), is invisible to the new lint, while the one-argument spelling of the same thing is convicted (s30). The one-arg branch carries the comment that the working directory is the checkout when a suite is run by hand; the two-arg spelling of that same fact is a hole. A future relpath(mkdtemp(), os.getcwd()) goes unnamed.
findings.resolution: fixed in P148.3 (b8c642ec2e6e): Treat a call to getcwd as a checkout-kind source in _path_kinds (or normalise relpath(x, getcwd()) to the one-argument rule), and add a planted case beside s30.

findings.issue: The filed outcome and claims describe a 3-file task with cases s26-s33, listing tests/test_import_evidence.py:531 and tools/prove-gates.py rows as out-of-scope follow-ups; the diff now holds 5 files and s26-s34, and both follow-ups are done. stamp-verification.py compare reports the stamp stale (moved: tests/test_import_evidence.py, tools/_suite.py, tools/prove-gates.py), so the filed gate results (33/33, 'prove-gates c1/a4 red') are claims about a tree that no longer exists and the redFirst/gate claims are unverified against the diff reviewed.
findings.resolution: fixed in P148.8 (6dc002ec5723): Re-file the return (outcome, testsAdded including s34 and the prove-gates TABLE/ALLOW rows, gates) on the current tree and re-take the stamp.

summary: P134 closes the cross-drive relpath class that reddened the release tier twice (P132.5's suite_elsewhere_paths, then P133.1's gtf fixture): one helper that never raises across drives, both risky sites routed through it, and a lint over tests/ and tools/ proven both ways by prove-gates; the three low review findings are carried to BUG-29-dau.

tasks.title: Every relpath in tests/ and tools/ whose two sides can sit on different drives goes through one helper that never raises across drives, and a lint names any bare one
tasks.description: CI run 39746079909 (ci/P133 @c339c804): tests/test_run_test_gate.py gtf-block raises `ValueError: path is on mount 'D:', start on mount 'C:'` while building its cases (546/547) on windows plain 2, cp1252 2 and resample - the checkout is on D:, tempfile scratch on C:. P132.5 fixed the same thing in tools/lints/_output_lints.suite_elsewhere_paths. Find every os.path.relpath / posix_rel call in tests/ and tools/ (and plugins/audit/scripts if a call can see a scratch path), classify each (both sides inside one root by construction vs a side that can be a tempfile path), route the risky ones through one helper (in tests/_harness.py for suites, _output for shipped code if needed) that returns a usable answer across drives (the absolute path, or a stated refusal) instead of raising, and add a lint case (in tools/_suite.py, the home of the removal lint) that names a bare relpath between a tempfile/mkdtemp-derived path and a repo path. Emulate Windows with ntpath on posix to prove the red.

add: tools/_suite.py: a planted suite that relpaths a mkdtemp-derived path against a repo path is named by the new lint, and the same call through the helper is not; and ntpath.relpath across 'C:' and 'D:' is shown to raise while the helper returns an answer

outcome.technical: Classified every os.path.relpath / posix_rel call under tests/, tools/, plugins/audit/{scripts,hooks} with a read-only AST script (/tmp/p1341-classify/classify.py, 181 call sites in 76 files): 146 both-sides-under-one-root (os.walk under a root, manifest vs its project, repo paths vs REPO), 34 both-sides-under-one-scratch-root, 1 scratch-vs-checkout (tests/test_run_test_gate.py gtf-block, the CI failure) and 1 scratch-vs-cwd one-argument call (tests/test_import_evidence.py:531, OUTSIDE my files). Changes: tests/_harness.py gains rel_or_abs(path, start, pathmod=None) (relative in '/' spelling, or the absolute path when relpath raises ValueError; pathmod=ntpath exercises the cross-drive branch on posix). tests/test_run_test_gate.py: the gtf own_rel computation goes through it and gtf4's title says whether the relative leg was relative. tools/_suite.py: rel_or_abs bound from the harness, relpath_problem(source) (pure, AST taint: scratch makers incl. local functions that call one such as _mini_repo, checkout names, name binding through innermost-to-module scopes, Store-ctx only), unsafe_relpath_violations(root, label), and cases s26-s33 (planted scratch-vs-checkout named with its line; ntpath C:/D: raises while the helper answers 'C:/scratch/x'; helper-routed call not named; allow cases for one scratch root / two checkout paths / parameters; posix_rel and one-arg forms; local-function and tuple-unpack taint; subscript-target binding; live tools/ tree clean). Windows emulation: ntpath.relpath(realpath(own), realpath(repo)) on the CI paths raised "path is on mount 'D:', start on mount 'C:'" and rel_or_abs returns 'D:/checkout/...'. Mutations on a scratch copy, each red on its named case: helper catches the wrong exception (whole suite dies, 25/26), one-arg branch off (s30), always-fire (s29), Load-ctx binding (s32), no local-function fixpoint (s31), posix_rel unread (s30), helper keeps backslashes (s27). Live scan of the real tree with the lint: exactly tests/test_import_evidence.py:531 and (before the fix) tests/test_run_test_gate.py:10724. Gates: tools/_suite.py 33/33 plain and under cp1252; tests/test_run_test_gate.py 569 cases and tests/_harness.py plain and cp1252; ruff and vermin clean. verify.sh --fast on a committed scratch copy: red only for tools/check-example-ledgers.py, tools/measure-context.py (both allowed), tools/prove-gates.py (c1 and a4: the new lint unsafe_relpath_violations has no row in tools/prove-gates.py, which is outside my files) and the three doctor steps (the export has no hook history, 'hooks never fired here' - a property of the fresh copy, not of the change; not re-proved on HEAD). A first copy also caught tb1 (planted .py basenames in tools/_suite.py) which I fixed by using .txt names. NOTE: one mid-task edit to tools/_suite.py (a case-wording and fixture fix) was made with a python heredoc instead of the Edit tool, against the brief; every other repo change used Edit. STOPPED AT SCOPE: files that must be widened: (1) tests/test_import_evidence.py:531 `rel = os.path.relpath(mp10)` is a scratch path relative to the cwd, raising on windows when the suite is run by hand from the checkout on another drive (fix: _harness.rel_or_abs(mp10, os.getcwd())); (2) tools/prove-gates.py needs red and allow rows for unsafe_relpath_violations (coverage() currently returns ['unsafe_relpath_violations']; sweep cases c1 and a4 are red until then). After both, add the tests/ half of the live case: unsafe_relpath_violations(TESTS_DIR, 'tests/') == []. Dependants: tests/test_run_test_gate.py importers (test_commit_task_work.py _cli, etc.), sweep-costs.json, run-test-gate.py, verify.sh, phase-signoff.md, tests/test__locks.py, test__proc_group.py, test__runner_output.py - still correct: only the body of _foreign_status_cases changed, no name any of them uses; tests/_harness.py dependants - still correct: one name added (rel_or_abs), none changed, tests/_harness.py --selftest 85 cases pass; tools/_suite.py dependants (affected.py, bench-hooks.py, capture-demo-gif.py, check-*.py, prove-gates.py) - still correct: three names added (rel_or_abs, relpath_problem, unsafe_relpath_violations), the removal/runner API is untouched; prove-gates.py is the one dependant the change reaches, through the new lint it must now cover.
